amendments.because: A fixed size and every round's own summary forever cannot both hold; the owner's goal is never hitting the limit
amendments.done_when: The pull request keeps per-round time summaries rather than every event, so a long item never reaches the body limit and keeps its whole round history

done_when: The pull request time record has a fixed size limit: it keeps a time summary for each of the recent rounds and folds older rounds into one totals line, so a long item never reaches the body limit and the board still shows its total time

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Not done
`_compact` folds records only when their worker `round` is less than the maximum worker round. Forge also supports multiple review rounds from repeated `forge close` calls without another worker turn (`test_item_time_history.py:379`); those review results all retain the same worker round and remain in the record. On a long item, they can grow past the body budget. `_bounded_body` then deletes event rows without folding their time into the summary, so a fresh clone can lose the item's total time.
findings.title: Not done: The pull request time record has a fixed size limit

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
The proof creates 200 distinct worker rounds, then checks that the recent lines have round numbers. It neither exercises multiple review rounds within one worker turn nor checks that each recent line contains a time summary. It therefore passes with the unbounded same-worker record above and would also pass if recent round times disappeared.

stop.reason: Owner chose one more round: fold by the number of records, not by building round, so repeated closes in one round also fold; the test adds many reviews in one round and checks each recent line has its time summary.

why: A long item's pull request time record grows toward GitHub's 64 KB body limit, and Forge trims older time detail from about round 16
